valuation_philosophy: CSU is a hyper-compounder / serial acquirer of vertical market software (VMS) businesses. Traditional organic-growth DCF understates value because CSU continuously reinvests FCFA2S into new acquisitions at 20-30% IRR hurdle rates, compounding intrinsic value per share over time. This model uses FCFA2S (Free Cash Flow Available to Shareholders - CSU management's preferred intrinsic value metric) as the primary FCF driver, projecting growth from a normalised base that blends FY2025 management FCFA2S ($1,683M) with the improving Q1 2026 trajectory. The DCF captures the capital deployment flywheel: growth rates reflect both organic portfolio growth (currently ~4-6% reported) AND the compounding benefit of reinvesting FCFA2S into new VMS acquisitions. WACC is set to reflect risk-adjusted returns for a diversified, recurring-revenue software conglomerate with moderate leverage.

inputs.base_fcfa2s_description: Normalised Year-0 FCFA2S: blends FY2025 management FCFA2S ($1,683M, +14.4% YoY) with Q1 2026 run-rate improvement. LTM FCFA2S (Q2 2025 through Q1 2026) = $2,323M but includes one elevated quarter (Q1 2026 OCF $897M). $1,900M represents a conservative normalised base.
inputs.net_debt_description: Q1 2026: Total debt $5,122M (CSI carrying $2,613M + WR $2,509M) minus cash $3,010M. Excludes IRGA liability (~$1,234M at Dec 2025) which is a separate contingent obligation.
inputs.irga_liability_note: IRGA liability (Topicus Joday Group put option) was ~$1,234M at Dec 31, 2025 with $775M classified as current. This contingent obligation is NOT included in net debt for this DCF but represents additional financial risk. Including it would reduce intrinsic values by approximately $58/share USD ($83/share CAD).
inputs.fcf_metric: FCFA2S (Free Cash Flow Available to Shareholders): CSU management's preferred intrinsic value metric. Calculated as operating cash flow minus maintenance CapEx minus lease payments. More conservative than simple OCF minus CapEx. CSI-shareholder-attributable portion only (excludes Topicus/Lumine NCI shares).

historical_growth.eps_note: GAAP EPS distorted by non-cash charges: FY2025 $24.15 impacted by $440M IRGA revaluation charge and $260M Asseco reclassification loss. LTM EPS = Q2+Q3+Q4 2025 + Q1 2026 = $35.06. GAAP CAGRs are not meaningful.
historical_growth.equity_cagr_note: Equity CAGRs inflated by acquisition leverage (book value grows with acquired intangibles). Not used as primary valuation driver.
historical_growth.growth_rate_selection_notes: FCFA2S 5yr CAGR of 11.2% is depressed by FY2021-22 weakness (Topicus spinout, Altera drag). 3yr CAGR of 25.4% reflects the acceleration. 6yr CAGR of 19.1% provides the best long-run estimate. Base case Year 1 growth of 18% reflects: (a) strong Q1 2026 M&A pipeline ($1.6B deployed/committed in Q1 alone); (b) improving organic growth to 4-6%; (c) Topicus/Lumine inorganic European expansion. Decelerates as deployment scale increases.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: FCFA2S 5yr CAGR (11.2%) diverges significantly from Revenue 5yr CAGR (24.0%) - divergence of 114%. However, this is expected and not a data quality flag: FCFA2S growth was compressed in FY2021-22 by Topicus spinout, Altera drag, and NCI adjustments. The 3yr CAGR of 25.4% and 6yr CAGR of 19.1% are more representative of forward trajectory. Revenue growth overstates FCFA2S growth due to the heavy reinvestment of cash into acquisitions (EV-dilutive at cost but value-creating at IRR).

base.notes: Normalised FCFA2S base of $1,900M grows at 18% in Y1, reflecting record Q1 2026 acquisition pipeline and improving organic growth trend, decelerating to 12% by Y5 as deployment scale increases ROIC pressure. WACC 10% appropriate for established serial acquirer with investment-grade credit quality and diversified VMS revenue base.

bull.notes: Record Q1 2026 acquisition pace ($1.6B in 4 months) sustained throughout 2026-2027. PEMS strategy adds capital deployment venue for large opportunities. Topicus (Q1 2026 +36% YoY USD) and Lumine continue aggressive European/telecom VMS consolidation. Organic growth improves to 6-8% as AI workflow integration monetises. Mark Miller proves a capable steward of the Leonard model. Lower WACC reflects premium compounder quality.

bear.notes: Leadership transition causes cultural disruption. PE competition (Vista, Thoma Bravo, Hg) severely compresses acquisition IRRs, slowing FCFA2S redeployment to 12% Y1. PEMS Sabre investment disappoints and signals strategy drift. FX-adjusted organic growth stays at 2%. Altera remains structural drag. Higher WACC reflects governance risk post-Leonard and PEMS uncertainty.

market_metrics_at_current_price.observation: At CAD $2,818, CSU trades at ~25x FY2025 management FCFA2S ($1,683M) - below its historical 30-55x range. The stock has de-rated ~47% from its all-time high of ~CAD $5,300 in 2024. On LTM FCFA2S ($2,323M), the market P/FCF is only 18x. This suggests CSU is at the low end of or below its historical valuation range, potentially offering value for long-term holders. The de-rating reflects: (1) Mark Leonard's complete Board departure; (2) PEMS strategy uncertainty; (3) 'SaaSpocalypse' software sector sentiment; (4) FCFA2S growth deceleration to 14% in FY2025.

csu_specific_notes.serial_acquirer_model: CSU does not grow organically - it acquires VMS businesses and holds them forever. The 'growth rate' in this DCF is driven primarily by redeployment of FCFA2S into acquisitions at 20-30% IRR hurdle rates. The Year 1-5 growth rates represent FCFA2S compounding from acquisitions (inorganic) plus portfolio organic growth (~4-6% reported). This is fundamentally different from a product-company DCF.
csu_specific_notes.pems_strategy: The new PEMS (Permanent Engaged Minority Shareholder) strategy allows CSU to deploy capital into very large businesses (e.g. Sabre Corporation 12.7% stake) where full acquisition is impractical. This is unproven at scale and not explicitly modeled in the DCF. Success would be upside to the bull case; failure would be consistent with the bear case.
csu_specific_notes.share_count_static: CSU has not repurchased or issued material shares since IPO. 21.192 million shares outstanding since at least 2015. No dilution expected.
csu_specific_notes.asseco_poland: 23.14% equity method stake in Asseco Poland (carrying value $590M, fair value $872M at Q1 2026). The $282M embedded unrealized gain is not reflected in the DCF but represents additional NAV per share of ~$13 USD (~$19 CAD). This is a conservative omission.
csu_specific_notes.mark_leonard_departure: Mark Leonard completed his departure from the Board of Directors at the May 15, 2026 AGM. He remains an advisor focused on PEMS. Mark Miller (President since September 2025, 30+ years at CSI/Volaris) leads the company. The bear case explicitly assigns higher WACC to reflect this governance transition risk.
csu_specific_notes.dividend: CSU pays a quarterly dividend of $1.00/share ($4.00/yr USD, ~$85M annually). This is ~5% of FCFA2S and is not separately modeled - it is captured within the FCFA2S definition.
csu_specific_notes.irga_liability: The IRGA (Investment Risk and Gain Account) liability related to Topicus Joday Group put option was ~$1,234M at Dec 31, 2025. This is excluded from net debt for DCF purposes (consistent with prior model) but represents a material contingent obligation. Investors should note that including IRGA in net debt would reduce intrinsic values by approximately $58/share USD ($83/share CAD) across all scenarios.
csu_specific_notes.ltm_fcfa2s_note: The LTM FCFA2S of $2,323M (Q2 2025 through Q1 2026) is elevated because Q1 is CSU's seasonally strongest OCF quarter and Q1 2026 benefited from record acquisition activity. The normalised base of $1,900M used in the DCF provides a more conservative starting point.
